source.prompt: (the red-tail's) A red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis), one adult bird soaring in mid-air, wings fully spread out flat to the sides and symmetrical, about 125 cm wingspan and 55 cm long, shaped to read from below and from above. Broad rounded wings with a straight leading edge and five separated, fingered primary feathers at each wingtip. Short, broad brick-red tail fanned wide into a rounded fan. Legs and feet tucked up under the body. Big rounded head and short hooked bill projecting ahead of the wings. Pale underwing with a dark leading-edge bar and a dark wrist mark, pale breast with a dark belly band. Not an eagle, not a falcon. Single bird, no base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: Ambient flight mesh as the hawk's and the eagle's: body and head from the generated mesh (feet and tail deleted, head reshaped, pitched 12 degrees nose-down); long narrow straight gull wings tapering to a pointed tip (arm raised 6 degrees, hand lowered 6), no fingers, a short square tail, a slim head projecting well ahead, a stout lofted gull bill with a gonys bulge and hooked tip; the wings, tail and bill lofted per tier in rows and stations placed on the field marks (lod2 wings 2.5x thicker). Tier switches suggested at 60 and 200 m (not wired). GLB 302,028 bytes.

rig: bird rig template, flight mesh, exactly as client/assets/redtail.glb (the client draws the raptors with the hawk's soaring and the gulls with the vulture's circling glides): PART BODY 0, TAIL 3 (pivot at the tail root), HEAD 6 (head, neck and bill, pivot at the neck's base), WING_L/R 4/5 (the arm, pivot at the shoulder, weight ramped in over the wing root), HAND_L/R 9/10 (pivot at the wrist, weight ramped over the hand); collapse 0 (the wings never fold). extras.rig keys as the hawk's: kind 'bird', wing (shoulder [0.071, 0.11, 0.02]), wrist [0.294, 0.133, 0.02], tail [0.0, 0.08, -0.095], head [0.0, 0.099, 0.181], span_m 1.4, dihedral_deg -1.8 (shoulder to wingtip). Origin 0.11 m below the shoulder line. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Field marks: white head, body and tail; pale grey mantle and upperwing with a white trailing edge; the wingtips grey like the mantle (a shade darker) with small white tip spots; the underwing white with pale grey flight feathers; a yellow bill with a red gonys spot (lod0); a dark eye. Reads as a large pale gull with no black in the wingtips at every tier, from above and below. Still open: the body is the red-tail's narrowed and flattened, still a little stocky for a gull; the wingtip pattern is simplified to a slightly darker grey tip with two white spots; the red gonys spot is lod0 only; no winter head smudging (adults in winter are dusky-headed), no immature plumages (the brown-grey first-winter birds are the ones most often seen); no legs (tucked).
